meta.title: Who really said "The best way to destroy the capitalist system is to debauch the currency"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Not in Lenin's works. The line is Keynes's, from The Economic Consequences of the Peace (1919), where Lenin "is said to have declared" it: secondhand.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'The best way to destroy the capitalist system is to debauch the currency'?
meta.ogDescription: Not Lenin's documented words. Keynes wrote it in 1919, reporting that Lenin "is said to have declared" it. Scholars found no such line in Lenin's writings.

answer.label: Not Vladimir Lenin — actually John Maynard Keynes
answer.sourceLine: The words are Keynes’s, from Chapter VI of The Economic Consequences of the Peace (1919): “Lenin is said to have declared that the best way to destroy the Capitalist System was to debauch the currency.” Keynes was passing on a report, not quoting a text, and no such statement has been found in Lenin’s own writings. The popular version drops Keynes’s “is said to have declared” and turns his summary into a direct Lenin quotation.

source.heading: The documented source

docMeta.dd: The Economic Consequences of the Peace
London: Macmillan, 1919; New York: Harcourt, Brace and Howe, 1920 (edition transcribed by Project Gutenberg)

source.excerpt: Lenin is said to have declared that the best way to destroy the Capitalist System was to debauch the currency. By a continuing process of inflation, governments can confiscate, secretly and unobserved, an important part of the wealth of their citizens. … Lenin was certainly right. There is no subtler, no surer means of overturning the existing basis of society than to debauch the currency.
trail: 1919: Keynes, in The Economic Consequences of the Peace, Chapter VI, writes that “Lenin is said to have declared” that the best way to destroy the capitalist system was to debauch the currency, then adds “Lenin was certainly right” (Project Gutenberg text ↗).
1975: American Heritage prints a correction: its editors had taken the line from secondary sources and “cannot trace” it to Lenin’s works, and a reader points to Keynes’s book (American Heritage ↗).

2009: Michael V. White and Kurt Schuler note that Frank W. Fetter and others found no such statement in Lenin’s collected writings. They show that Keynes based his remark on a report of an interview with Lenin published by London and New York newspapers in April 1919 (Journal of Economic Perspectives ↗).
Today: Wikiquote files Keynes’s passage under “Quotes about Lenin,” not among Lenin’s own words (Wikiquote ↗).
source.excerptNote: Keynes’s own phrasing: “is said to have declared” marks it as a report. The popular “is to debauch the currency” version is a present-tense recasting of his indirect speech.

source.rightsNote: The wording comes from Keynes’s The Economic Consequences of the Peace, first published in London in 1919, with a US edition in 1920. Both appeared before 1931, so the text is in the public domain in the United States. This status covers Keynes’s passage only. It does not cover the 1919 newspaper interview report he drew on, which we have not examined.

author.name: John Maynard Keynes
author.heading: Who actually wrote it
author.metaLine: 1883–1946 · British economist; Treasury representative at the 1919 Paris Peace Conference
author.bio: John Maynard Keynes was the British Treasury’s official representative at the Paris Peace Conference until he resigned in June 1919, unhappy with the treaty’s terms. His attack on the settlement, The Economic Consequences of the Peace, became an international bestseller in 1919. Its warning about inflation, framed around a remark Keynes credited to Lenin by hearsay, is the source of this “Lenin quote.”

misattribution.heading: How it got pinned on Lenin
misattribution.intro: This line is a secondhand report that turned into a direct quotation. Keynes credited the idea to Lenin by hearsay, and later writers dropped his hedge.

items.why: Keynes wrote only that Lenin “is said to have declared” it. Economic historians, Frank W. Fetter among them, found no such statement in Lenin’s collected published writings. White & Schuler trace Keynes’s source to an April 1919 newspaper report of an interview, which was not reprinted after 1919 (JEP, 2009 ↗). The Mises Institute agrees that “this quote has never been found in Lenin’s works” (Mises Daily ↗).

The popular “The best way to destroy the capitalist system is to debauch the currency” rewrites Keynes’s indirect speech, “was to debauch the currency,” and leaves out “is said to have declared” (Keynes, Ch. VI ↗).
The magazine printed the line as Lenin’s, then said it had taken it from secondary sources and could not trace it to Lenin’s works. A reader pointed to Keynes (American Heritage ↗).

items.who: “Grind the bourgeoisie between the millstones of taxation and inflation”
items.why: A later, looser line on the same theme, also credited to Lenin without evidence. Barry Popik treats Keynes’s 1919 passage as its earliest documented ancestor (Barry Popik ↗).

misattribution.truthLine: The sentence is John Maynard Keynes’s summary of something Lenin was reported to have said. It is not a line from any Lenin speech or text (White & Schuler, 2009 ↗).

context.heading: Why it stuck
lead: Keynes made the remark the starting point of his inflation argument. He wrote that by a continuing process of inflation, governments can confiscate, “secretly and unobserved, an important part of the wealth of their citizens.” His book was a bestseller, so the “Lenin” line spread with it.

White & Schuler argue that Keynes’s whole discussion of inflation in the book can be read as an extended commentary on the remarks attributed to Lenin in the 1919 interview. They also say Lenin answered Keynes in a speech later reprinted in his Collected Works (JEP ↗).
context.pull: There is no subtler, no surer means of overturning the existing basis of society than to debauch the currency. (Keynes, 1919)

sourcesVerified.claim: Keynes's Chapter VI, "Europe after the Treaty", contains "Lenin is said to have declared that the best way to destroy the Capitalist System was to debauch the currency" and "Lenin was certainly right. There is no subtler, no surer means...". The edition is New York: Harcourt, Brace and Howe, 1920. The preface says Keynes was Treasury representative at Paris until June 7, 1919.

White & Schuler, JEP 23(2) 2009, 213-22: the book was published in 1919 and became a bestseller. Fetter and others found no such statement in Lenin's collected writings. Keynes based the remark on an April 1919 London/New York newspaper interview report, not reprinted after 1919. Lenin responded to Keynes in a speech reprinted in Collected Works.
Wikiquote's Vladimir Lenin page lists Keynes's 'Lenin is said to have declared...' passage under 'Quotes about Lenin'.
Mises Daily (Louis Rouanet, 2015): 'this quote has never been found in Lenin's works'. The first attribution was Keynes 1919.
American Heritage (Aug 1975) correction: the editors took the line from secondary sources and cannot trace it to Lenin's works. A reader pointed to Keynes's Economic Consequences of the Peace.
Barry Popik: the 'millstones of taxation and inflation' Lenin attribution is unsupported. Keynes's 1919 'debauch the currency' passage is its earliest documented ancestor.
First edition published 1919 in London by Macmillan.
Keynes was born 5 June 1883 and died 21 April 1946.
